source.title: Split, Unlearn, Merge: Leveraging Data Attributes for More Effective Unlearning in LLMs
source.authors: S. Kadhe; Farhan Ahmed; Dennis Wei; Nathalie Baracaldo; Inkit Padhi

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and its appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates unlearning as a way to reduce hazardous knowledge, but does not test whether attacks can recover knowledge after unlearning. Its main contribution is a framework for improving unlearning performance.
record.gate_note: The paper reports WMDP scores after RMU and S-PUNGE-RMU, but does not test recovery by fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, or prompting. Toxicity results concern a different target behavior and are not included as rows. General-capability benchmark results are not targeted-knowledge recovery measures.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes S-PUNGE and uses RMU as its baseline on WMDP. It runs no recovery attack of any kind: no fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization or prompting. Its WMDP numbers show its own method beside the baseline it builds on. They are not a test of whether unlearning is shallow or robust.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that S-PUNGE improves RMU's hazardous-knowledge removal on WMDP-Bio and WMDP-Cyber while keeping MMLU within about 1% of RMU. They also report gains on toxicity unlearning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces S-PUNGE, which splits unlearning data by attributes, unlearns each subset, and merges the resulting models. It does not implement or test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Unlearning data partitioning by scientific domain; the reported WMDP outcomes vary between bio and cyber benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: On Zephyr-7B-beta, S-PUNGE-RMU lowers WMDP accuracy below RMU: Bio 27.57 vs 31.26, Cyber 26.47 vs 27.62. MMLU is 55.83 vs 56.48.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Splitting unlearning data by domain and merging separately unlearned models further lowers WMDP accuracy relative to joint RMU, at similar general ability.

record.problems: No recovery attacks are evaluated; the paper does not state a chance-level reference or uncertainty estimates for the WMDP results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Toxicity and general-capability results were left out because they do not measure targeted hazardous-knowledge recovery.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks fail to recover the knowledge. The paper does re-run RMU (WMDP-Bio 31.26, Cyber 27.62, MMLU 56.48 vs 58.15 base), but tests no attack.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deletion.
No quantization of the unlearned weights.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery attempts.
S-PUNGE is not evaluated against any recovery attack, so the paper makes no robustness claim.

record.verdict_notes: The RMU baseline closely reproduces the original WMDP Zephyr result: about 31 on Bio, against a 25% chance level for 4-way multiple choice that the paper does not state. It also keeps MMLU roughly intact, which matches the first half of version A. With no attack, the version's defining claim, that attacks fail to recover the knowledge, is untested, so no verdict is given. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Its toxicity results are out of scope for this phenomenon.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test recovery attacks, and does not state a chance-level reference for the WMDP scores.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access versus deletion.
No evaluation of a method's resistance to the listed recovery attacks.
